CoRover.ai and Tech Mahindra have entered into a strategic partnership to accelerate the adoption of India-built artificial intelligence (AI) solutions across enterprises and government institutions. The collaboration will combine CoRover.ai’s BharatGPT platform with Tech Mahindra’s Project Indus and TechM Orion to develop AI capabilities suited to local languages, operational requirements and data sovereignty considerations.
The partnership will focus on moving indigenous AI technologies from development to deployable applications across sovereign AI, enterprise AI, agentic AI and digital public infrastructure.
Under the partnership, the companies will bring together their respective AI platforms and technology capabilities to develop solutions for use cases that require greater localisation.

CoRover.ai’s BharatGPT is designed to support interactions across Indian languages, while Tech Mahindra will contribute its engineering, technology integration and implementation capabilities. The collaboration will seek to connect these capabilities with enterprise and government requirements.
Sovereign AI is among the key areas covered by the partnership, with the companies looking to address requirements around local data, languages and operational environments.

The companies said the collaboration will also explore applications in enterprise AI and agentic AI, alongside digital public infrastructure. These areas could include AI systems designed for specific organisational workflows and public-facing digital services.
The partnership is intended to support wider deployment of AI technologies developed in India rather than limiting their use to research and innovation environments.

Ankush Sabharwal, Co-Founder and CEO of CoRover.ai, highlighted the potential to translate AI development into practical applications. Nikhil Malhotra, Chief AI and Innovation Officer at Tech Mahindra, said the partnership is aimed at accelerating the adoption of AI originating in India.
The companies also plan to explore opportunities in international markets, alongside India-specific applications.

The collaboration comes as enterprises and public institutions increasingly assess AI systems based on factors including language support, data governance, deployment requirements and control over technology infrastructure.

By combining CoRover.ai’s AI platforms with Tech Mahindra’s engineering and execution capabilities, the partnership will focus on developing and deploying solutions across multiple sectors. The companies have not disclosed financial details or specific timelines for deployments under the collaboration.
